scoring_justification: Checker cannot recompute DFT Fermi levels; scores structural relations (CBM alignment, monotonicity) against agent's own pristine gap with tolerances.

hidden_assets.purpose: paper-reported Fermi level table and pristine gap used as tolerance reference for structural checks
hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper Supporting Information Figure S11 and DFT PBE band gap for monolayer MoS2 (value 1.68 eV, from DFT calculations in the paper)
hidden_assets.generation_method: extracted from the paper's reported table (Fig. S11) and band gap from the paper's pristine MoS2 calculation (1.68 eV). The gold values are used to validate the oracle; the checker itself uses only structural relations and does not compare to these exact values.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact values reported in the paper's supporting information, confirmed against the referenced figure and table.

outputs.description: Pristine monolayer MoS2 band gap (CBM−VBM) in eV, used as alignment reference.
Fermi level positions relative to the valence band maximum for each defect type and Na count.

output_contract.notes: The checker uses the agent's own pristine band gap to align the Fermi levels and verifies that EF_minus_VBM ≥ pristine CBM only for S5|7 with 2 Na, and never decreases with Na count for any defect. Tolerance of 0.2 eV accounts for code-to-code variation.

steps.description: Check that the computed pristine band gap is within a plausible PBE range for monolayer MoS2.
Verify that for S5|7 with 2 Na, EF_minus_VBM is at least the pristine CBM within 0.2 eV tolerance.
Verify that for all other configurations, EF_minus_VBM is below the pristine CBM within 0.2 eV tolerance.
Check that for each defect type, EF_minus_VBM does not decrease significantly (within 0.2 eV tolerance) as Na count increases.
